disclaimer: Educational only — not a fatwa. Verify with Qur'an, Sunnah, and a local scholar.

seeker.label: Junior · Seeker
seeker.goal: Know Allah, the pillars of iman and Islam, the Messenger ﷺ, adab, and hope in the hereafter.

u1-l1.title: Allah is One
u1-l1.summary: Tawhid is the heart of Islam: Allah alone is worthy of worship.
points: Allah created the heavens and the earth and everything between them.
Nothing is like Him — He is unique in His names and attributes.
We direct prayer, hope, and fear to Him alone.
Junior action: before a task, say Bismillah with presence of heart.

u1-l2.title: Allah sees and knows
u1-l2.summary: Allah’s knowledge covers what we show and what we hide.
points: He knows the secret and what is more hidden.
This knowledge is mercy — it invites honesty, not despair.
Junior practice: correct a small action when no one is watching, for Allah’s sake.

ayah.en: We are closer to him than his jugular vein.

u2-l1.title: Belief map (overview)
u2-l1.summary: Iman includes belief in Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and decree.
points: The Hadith of Jibril teaches the pillars of iman clearly.
Belief shapes character: hope, patience, and responsibility.
Learn the names of the pillars before deep debates.

u2-l2.title: Prophets and the Last Day (gentle)
u2-l2.summary: Allah sent messengers with one core message; we will meet Allah.
points: Prophets called to worship Allah alone.
Muhammad ﷺ is the final messenger.
Remembering the Last Day softens the heart toward good deeds.

u3-l1.title: Shahadah to Hajj (map)
u3-l1.summary: The five pillars structure a Muslim’s public and private life.
points: Shahadah, salah, zakah, sawm, and Hajj (for those who can).
Start with what you can do with consistency.
Pillars are doors of mercy, not slogans.

u3-l2.title: Living words — Commands
u3-l2.summary: Allah addresses the believers with practical guidance.
points: “O you who believe” verses call to action with faith.
Hear a command, take one small step the same day.
Verify understanding with reliable teachers when unsure.

u4-l1.title: Who is Muhammad ﷺ?
u4-l1.summary: The Messenger is the best example in character and guidance.
points: He taught with gentleness and clarity.
Loving him means following what he brought.
Send salawat with presence, not only habit.

u4-l2.title: Samiʿnā wa aṭaʿnā
u4-l2.summary: We hear and we obey — the posture of the believer.
points: Listening precedes arguing.
Obedience is tied to knowledge and sincerity.
Junior action: obey one clear good instruction today without delay.

ayah.en: …they say: We hear and we obey.

u5-l1.title: Truth, kindness, clean tongue
u5-l1.summary: Adab is part of iman lived outward.
points: Speak truthfully; avoid harming with words.
Kindness is not weakness.
A clean tongue protects the heart and relationships.

u5-l2.title: Parents and teachers
u5-l2.summary: Respect for parents and teachers is a path of barakah.
points: Lower the wing of humility to parents.
Thank those who teach you even one ayah.
Junior action: one gentle service or kind word to a parent or elder.

u6-l1.title: Death is a door — hope and work
u6-l1.summary: Remembering death wakes the heart without despair.
points: Everyone will taste death; preparation is daily good.
Hope in Allah’s mercy and do the next right deed.
Furnish the grave with salah, Qur’an, and character — educational reminder only.

new-muslim.label: New Muslim · Practice
new-muslim.goal: Build purification and prayer with confidence and community.

jh-u1-l1.title: You are not alone
jh-u1-l1.summary: Entering Islam is a beginning of mercy and learning.
points: Allah is Forgiving and Merciful to the sincere.
Ask questions; good teachers welcome learners.
One step at a time is a prophetic way.

jh-u1-l2.title: Shahādah — living meaning
jh-u1-l2.summary: The testimony is belief, word, and life direction.
points: No deity worthy of worship except Allah.
Muhammad ﷺ is His messenger.
Renew intention when you learn a new practice.

jh-u2-l1.title: Cleanliness is half of faith
jh-u2-l1.summary: Purity prepares the body and heart for worship.
points: Learn wudu step by step with a reliable guide.
Remove impurities from body, clothes, and place of prayer.
When unsure, ask — do not guess rulings.

jh-u2-l2.title: Purification and prayer foundations
jh-u2-l2.summary: Salah needs purity as a condition in normal cases.
points: Connect wudu to the next prayer time.
Keep a small clean space for prayer if possible.
Educational tools are not a substitute for local teaching.

jh-u3-l1.title: Five prayers — the spine of the day
jh-u3-l1.summary: Salah structures time around remembrance of Allah.
points: Learn the names and rough times of the five prayers.
Pray on time as best you can; improve gradually.
Use an azan alert as a helper, not a judge.

jh-u3-l2.title: What to recite first
jh-u3-l2.summary: Start with Al-Fatiha and short surahs.
points: Al-Fatiha is the opening of every rakʿah.
Add short surahs as you memorize.
Tajweed grows with listening and gentle practice.

jh-u3-l3.title: Check yourself kindly
points: Review one part of prayer each week.
Celebrate consistency more than perfection.
Seek a local class when ready.

jh-u4-l1.title: Halal daily choices
jh-u4-l1.summary: Faith appears in food, speech, and earnings at a basic level.
points: Avoid clear haram as you learn.
When food is unclear, choose the safer known option.
Honesty in speech is part of daily practice.

jh-u4-l2.title: A calm Muslim day
jh-u4-l2.summary: Morning and evening remembrances protect the heart.
points: Learn a short morning and evening adhkar set.
Keep them brief so you continue.
Pair adhkar with an existing habit (after Fajr, after Maghrib).

daily.label: Daily · Consistency
daily.goal: Qur’an craft, reflection, and steady deeds.

hs-u1-l1.title: One rule, one ayah
hs-u1-l1.summary: Tajweed improves through small, repeated steps.
points: Pick one tajweed rule and one ayah.
Listen, then repeat slowly.
Use Companion Lab tools when you want practice tools.

hs-u1-l2.title: Listening lab
points: Choose a measured reciter.
Shadow-read without rushing.
Record only for private improvement if it helps you.

hs-u2-l1.title: Deepen study path
points: Read a short passage with a reliable translation.
Write one action sentence.
Avoid hot debates until foundations are firm.

hs-u2-l2.title: Names of Allah
points: Learn a few names with meaning and living effect.
Ar-Rahman invites mercy in your speech.
Al-Hakim invites trust when plans change.

hs-u3-l1.title: Weekly review
hs-u3-l1.summary: Beloved deeds are consistent, even if small.
points: Review salah consistency once a week.
Review one Qur’an habit.
Thank Allah for progress; seek forgiveness for gaps.

dai.label: Daʿi · Transmission
dai.goal: Call to Allah with wisdom, adab, and clear limits.

dai-u1-l1.title: Definition and intention
dai-u1-l1.summary: Daʿwah is invitation to Allah, not to the self.
points: Intention: guidance and clarity for people.
Ego ruins the message.
Begin with your own practice.

dai-u1-l2.title: Adab of the caller
dai-u1-l2.summary: Wisdom and beautiful preaching are commanded.
points: Qur’an 16:125 sets the tone.
Listen before you answer.
Anger is not a proof.

ayah.en: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction…

dai-u2-l1.title: Seerah as method
dai-u2-l1.summary: The Prophet’s method is patience, clarity, and mercy.
points: Study how he taught different people differently.
Public courage and private gentleness both matter.
Seerah is not entertainment only — it is method.

dai-u2-l2.title: Living transmission
dai-u2-l2.summary: Share what you know with honesty about limits.
points: Say “Allah knows best” when unsure.
Point to scholars for rulings.
This site is educational — not a fatwa service.

dai-u3-l1.title: Content craft with care
dai-u3-l1.summary: Media can remind or mislead — choose carefully.
points: Prefer clear Qur’an and authentic reminders.
Avoid mockery and clickbait about sacred matters.
Design for understanding, not performance.
